topic: The Construction of the Great Wall

text.content: For thousands of years, the farmers living in the rich, northern valleys of China faced a terrible threat. The groups of fierce warriors who frequently rode horses across the northern borders to steal food and attack villages were known as nomadic tribes. To protect their land from these fast, dangerous horsemen, local Chinese leaders began building tall barriers out of dirt and wood along the border.

In 221 BC, the different regions of China were finally united into a single, powerful empire. To protect his new, massive country, the leader ordered that all the smaller, disconnected barriers be joined together into one massive, continuous wall. The fierce leader who originally ordered this unbelievable building project was China’s first emperor. His name was Qin Shi Huang.

Building a wall that stretched for thousands of kilometers was incredibly difficult. The ancient builders did not have modern machines, so everything had to be done by human hands. Millions of soldiers and poor farmers were forced to work in freezing mountains and hot deserts. They built the early wall by tightly packing local dirt and heavy stones together inside wooden frames, a method known as rammed earth.

Hundreds of years later, another group of leaders decided to completely rebuild the wall to make it even stronger. Instead of just packing dirt, they used millions of heavy stone bricks to create a massive military fortress. They added tall watchtowers so soldiers could safely shoot arrows at invading enemies. The powerful ruling family that completely rebuilt the wall using these strong bricks was the Ming Dynasty.

Today, the Great Wall of China is the longest human-made structure in the history of the world. While it is no longer used for military protection, it is an incredibly popular tourist attraction that brings millions of visitors to China every year. Although the natural weather has damaged some older sections, the brick walls built by the Ming Dynasty still stand strong, snaking beautifully across the green mountain tops.

options.text: The danger of horsemen and the first simple barriers
The first emperor and his order to connect the wall
The difficult human labor and the packed dirt method
Rebuilding a stronger fortress using stone bricks
The modern survival and tourism of the famous structure
The high cost of buying a tourist ticket today
How modern machines quickly rebuild the broken walls

questions.prompt: Who were the fierce warriors that frequently rode horses across the northern borders to attack farming villages?
Who was the fierce leader that originally ordered all the smaller, disconnected barriers be joined together?
What was the powerful ruling family that completely rebuilt the wall using strong bricks and tall watchtowers?

stage_3_logic.instructions: Are the following statements True, False, or Not Given according to the text?

questions.prompt: The ancient builders used modern construction machines to lift the heavy stones into the mountains.
questions.explanation: Paragraph C clearly states: 'The ancient builders did not have modern machines, so everything had to be done by human hands.'

questions.prompt: The early version of the wall was built by tightly packing local dirt and heavy stones inside wooden frames.
questions.explanation: Paragraph C confirms this, describing how they built the wall by 'tightly packing local dirt and heavy stones together inside wooden frames.'

questions.prompt: The Great Wall of China is the most expensive building project in the history of the world.
questions.explanation: The text mentions that it is the longest human-made structure in the world, but it provides no information comparing its financial cost to other historical building projects.
